# Globlin

> A Windows tray app that watches your globally installed npm and bun packages and tells you the moment one falls behind. One click to update, no installer, a single portable 1.7 MB .exe, free and open source under GPL-3.0.

Global command-line tools installed with `npm install -g` or `bun add -g` go stale silently — nothing tells you a CLI is six versions behind until a command breaks. Globlin sits in the Windows tray, checks the registry on a schedule (every six hours by default), and shows exactly which packages are outdated. Clicking a row updates that package; Update all runs the outdated ones as a queue.

It never updates a package on its own. It can update itself unattended, but that setting is off by default and every download is verified against a published SHA-256 checksum before anything is replaced. Packages can be ignored, and an ignored package still shows its version but is never checked or notified about. A desktop notification fires only when the set of outdated packages changes.

Globlin needs no runtime of its own — it drives whatever npm or bun is already installed. Windows 10 and 11 only; there is no macOS or Linux build. Configuration lives in `globlin.json` next to the executable, which makes the whole thing portable.

- [Latest release](https://github.com/TOR968/Globlin/releases/latest): `globlin.exe` and its `.sha256`
